source_text: Περὶ τοῦ μὴ δεῖν ἱερατικοὺς δανείζειν, καὶ τόκους, καὶ τὰς λεγόμενος ἡμιολίας λαμβάνειν. Ἐ ρ μ η ν ε ί α. Δέν πρέπει οἱ ἱερωμένοι νά δανείζουν καὶ νά λαμβάνουν διάφορα καὶ ἡμιολίας, ἤτοι τὸ μισὸν τοῦ ὅλου διαφόρου τῶν ἑκατόν, ἤτοι ἐξ νομίσματα ἢ γρόσια εἰς τὰ ἑκατόν, κατὰ τὸν παρόντα Κανόνα. Ὅρᾳ καὶ τὸν μδ΄. Ἀποστολικόν.
thought_title: Clergy must not lend at interest
orientation: The council is issuing a canon forbidding clergy from lending money at interest, followed by an interpretation explaining the rates.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the rule that priests must not lend, and take interest, and the so-called one-and-a-half rates. Interpretation. Priests must not lend and take various rates and one-and-a-half rates, that is, half of the whole rate of the hundred, that is, six coins or piasters per hundred, according to the present Canon. See also the 44th Apostolic Canon.

choices.why: The heading uses the adjective substantivally for clergy; 'priests' matches the interpretation's ἱερωμένοι.
The interpretation explains it as half of the whole rate, so the literal 'one-and-a-half' is kept.
In Byzantine Greek διάφορον means interest; 'rates' fits the plural and the explanation of percentages.
The Ottoman-era coin term is rendered by its standard English equivalent.

pass_b_english: Concerning the rule that clergy must not lend money, charge interest, or take what are called one-and-a-half rates. Interpretation. According to this present canon, clergy must not lend money and take interest and one-and-a-half rates—that is, half of the whole rate on a hundred, meaning six coins or piasters per hundred. See also Apostolic Canon 44.

problems.quote: and take rates and one-and-a-half rates
problems.why: English adds 'and take rates' before 'one-and-a-half rates', but source says 'take various [rates] and one-and-a-half rates'; 'διάφορα' means 'various' not 'rates'.
problems.fix: those in holy orders must not lend and take various rates and one-and-a-half rates
problems.ruling: διάφορα means 'various', not 'rates'; translator misread it as τόκον/διαφοράν, changing meaning.

edits.old: clergy must not lend money and take rates and one-and-a-half rates
edits.new: clergy must not lend money and take various rates and one-and-a-half rates

fixed: Added 'various' to match source 'διάφορα' ('various'), which the English omitted; the source says 'take various [rates] and one-and-a-half rates', not 'take rates and one-and-a-half rates'.

problems.why: ἱερατικούς means clergy generally, not priests specifically.
problems.fix: Concerning the rule that clergy must not lend money, charge interest, or take what are called one-and-a-half rates.
problems.ruling: ἱερατικοὺς = 'clerical ones/clergy', broader than 'priests'; source later uses ἱερωμένοι = 'ordained/ clergy' confirming scope.

problems.why: διάφορα here means 'interest' (different from principal), not 'various rates'.
problems.ruling: διάφορα means 'interest' (difference from principal), not 'various rates'; mistranslates key financial term.

fixed: ἱερατικούς means clergy generally, not priests specifically; changed to 'clergy'.
διάφορα here means interest, not various rates; changed to 'interest'.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'priests' not 'clergy'; ἱερατικός means priestly, not clergy generally.
last_rejected.ruling: ἱερατικός means 'priestly/clerical'; 'clergy' is within normal semantic range, not 'priests' specifically.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'six coins or groats,' not 'piasters'; πιάστρες is a later Ottoman coin, anachronistic here.
last_rejected.fix: six coins or groats per hundred
last_rejected.ruling: γρόσια commonly means piasters in Byzantine/post-Byzantine Greek; normal semantic range, not anachronistic for this text's era.
